Strike it, and metal turns\nstored elastic strain into regular motion.\n\nA Geiger counter is calm until a particle arrives. Its job is to\nlose the argument deliberately.\n\nA fuse protects a circuit by becoming the broken part. It is a promise that\nthere will be one cheap failure before there is one expensive fire.\n\nA pencil eraser does not delete graphite like a command. It grips or lifts\nloose graphite and can abrade the paper; correction often means damaging the\nsurface gently enough that the damage passes as repair.\n\nA phonograph needle wears down as it reads. Contact is how it learns the groove,\nand contact is also what spends it.\n\nA calibration weight is not useful because it does anything. It is useful\nbecause it keeps being the same amount of nothing in particular.\n\n\nANCIENT MEMORY TECHNOLOGIES\n---------------------------\n\nThe method of loci, or memory palace, is traditionally linked to Simonides of\nCeos. A remembered place becomes a filing system by turning facts into objects\nand placing them along a route.\n\nInca quipu used knotted cords to record information. The knots could encode\nnumbers, and scholars debate how much non-numeric information they carried.\nA knot can be a number before it becomes a sentence.\n\nWax tablets were reusable writing surfaces in the ancient Mediterranean world.\nThe stylus made a groove; the flat end could smooth the wax back out. Forgetting\nwas a physical gesture.\n\nTally sticks recorded debts by splitting one notched stick into two matching\nhalves. Trust lived in the fact that the broken pieces still fit.\n\n\nSIGNALS HIDING IN MEDIUMS\n-------------------------\n\nThe SOFAR channel is a deep ocean layer where sound can travel very long\ndistances because sound speed reaches a minimum and refracts sound back into\nthe channel.\n\nTree rings can preserve climate information, fires, disease, and hard years.\nA tree does not keep a diary; it changes diameter under pressure.\n\nIce cores trap old air in bubbles. Climate history can sit inside ice as\ncompressed atmosphere.\n\nRadiolarians are tiny marine organisms with intricate mineral skeletons. Their\nfossils can become signals in deep-sea sediment.\n\nMiyake events are sudden spikes in radioactive carbon found in tree rings,\nprobably caused by extreme solar particle events. A tree can remember the Sun\nthrowing something.\n\n\nMACHINES WITH A MORAL PROBLEM\n-----------------------------\n\nCharles Babbage's Difference Engine was designed to compute mathematical\ntables mechanically. It was a machine for removing human arithmetic errors,\nbut it became famous partly because it was not completed in his lifetime.\n\nThe Jacquard loom used punched cards to control woven patterns. A fabric\nmachine helped make the idea of programmable control feel physical.\n\nThe Apollo Guidance Computer used rope memory for fixed programs: wires threaded\nthrough or around magnetic cores represented bits. Software could be literally\nwoven.\n\nThe Therac-25 radiation therapy accidents showed that software timing, missing\ninterlocks, and operator trust can become dangerous together. A friendly\ninterface can hide a machine that needs harder skepticism.\n\nThe first mechanical escapements made clocks count regular releases of stored\nenergy. An escapement is a machine that advances by repeatedly saying no.\n\n\nSTABLE FACTS WITH COMMON TRAPS\n------------------------------\n\nThe Antikythera mechanism is not a clock in the ordinary household sense.\nCalling it a clock is poetic unless the exact mechanism is explained.\n\nSundial error is not proof the sundial is bad. \"Equation of time\" is the useful\nsearch phrase.\n\nQuipu were not simply \"Inca writing\" unless the claim is carefully hedged.\nThe numeric use is strong; the narrative-language question is debated.\n\nRope memory is not the same as magnetic core RAM. Rope memory was read-only\nprogram storage; core memory was rewritable working memory.\n\nThe SOFAR channel is not a radio channel. It is an acoustic waveguide in the\nocean.\n\nSacrificial anodes are not noble. They protect a more noble metal by being more\nreactive.\n\n\nOPEN QUESTIONS\n--------------\n\nWhy does a machine that says no at exactly the right interval feel more alive\nthan a machine that simply says yes?\n\nIs a memory palace a kind of body, or is it a place pretending to be a body?\n\nWhen a tool wears itself down while reading the world, is the wear a cost, a\nrecord, or both?\n\nWhy do humans trust devices more when the device has a ritual: strike the fork,\nalign the sextant, wind the watch, tare the scale?\n\nWhat is the difference between an honest error and a calibrated approximation?\n\nDoes a fuse fail, or does it succeed by being the one part that dies?\n\nWhy does woven software feel stranger than written software, even though both\nare patterns made durable?\n\nWhat kind of memory is a tree ring: observation, scar, or receipt?\n\n\nCLEAN LOOKUP HOOKS\n------------------\n\nAntikythera mechanism eclipse prediction gears\nequation of time sundial clock difference\nSimonides method of loci memory palace origin\nInca quipu numeric narrative information debate\nApollo Guidance Computer rope memory woven software\nSOFAR channel sound speed minimum ocean waveguide\nMiyake event carbon 14 tree rings solar particle\nBabbage Difference Engine unfinished lifetime\nJacquard loom punched cards programmable control\nsacrificial anode galvanic corrosion protects steel\nTherac-25 software interlock accidents summary\n\n\nRIFF HANDLES\n------------\n\nA dark box that sees by refusing light.\nA broken part hired in advance.\nA tree keeping solar weather in its rings.\nA knot that might be a number trying to become a sentence.\nA clock that moves because it is interrupted correctly.\nSoftware as thread, not text.\nA navigator holding an angle and pretending it is a place.\nA machine that keeps a promise by wearing out.\n"}
